content_html:
Silverfish often appear in bathrooms because they find moisture, narrow shelter, and materials containing starch or cellulose. Seeing one does not mean the bathroom is dirty; the most useful clue is whether persistent humidity, leaks, or condensation keep the space favorable.

Look for moisture that lingers after showers

Check ventilation, wall condensation, damp joints, and water around sinks or toilets. If the bathroom takes hours to dry, reducing moisture often matters more than treating each insect that appears.

Inspect cracks and gaps used as shelter

Separated baseboards, pipe penetrations, and gaps below cabinets provide darkness and shelter. Seal nonfunctional gaps after moisture is corrected without blocking ventilation or required access.

Reduce cardboard, paper, and accumulated debris

Stored paper, damp boxes, adhesives, and organic debris can provide food. Keep textiles dry and avoid storing cardboard directly on a damp floor or inside a cabinet with condensation.

Persistent activity can point to hidden moisture

If many silverfish appear across rooms after visible moisture is controlled, inspect for hidden leaks and nearby damp areas. Chemical treatment without correcting water and shelter usually provides only temporary results.
